lines: +summary: Fix NPE/CCE in `ReplaceSumWithStats` on nested SUM
@@ -1199,6 +1199,58 @@ GROUP BY gender HAVING max > 155000 or min > 36000 ORDER BY gender;
+// A group is down to one row by the time HAVING/ORDER BY is evaluated, so SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/PERCENTILE over an
+// aggregate alias return that one value unchanged. The next two must therefore agree row for row.
+SELECT gender, SUM(salary) AS s FROM test_emp WHERE gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY gender HAVING SUM(s) > 2000000 ORDER BY gender;
+SELECT gender, SUM(salary) AS s FROM test_emp WHERE gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY gender HAVING s > 2000000 ORDER BY gender;
+// the outer and inner aggregates need not match: only the outer one has to be an identity over a single value
+SELECT gender, MIN(salary) AS m FROM test_emp WHERE gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY gender HAVING AVG(m) > 25950 ORDER BY gender;
+// AVG is DOUBLE while MIN(<integer>) is not, so this pins down that dropping the wrapper keeps the HAVING
+// arithmetic on doubles: M only qualifies because 25945 / 2 is 12972.5 rather than 12972
+SELECT gender, MIN(salary) AS m FROM test_emp WHERE gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY gender HAVING AVG(m) / 2 > 12972 ORDER BY gender;
+SELECT gender, MIN(salary) AS m FROM test_emp WHERE gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY gender ORDER BY MIN(m);
